newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds close weaker amid supply concern.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds close weaker amid supply concern.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker in quiet trade on Monday, underperforming U.S. Treasuries, as recent Canadian dollar weakness and expectations of new supply weighed on the market, analysts said.

"It's a number of little things as opposed to anything hugely negative. I think it's just a weaker currency and supply concerns," said Cameron Laird, a bond porfolio manager with Zurich Canada Investment Management Ltd.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.55 to C$115.70 to yield 6.723 percent against the U.S. 30-year bonds, which fell 1/32 to yield 6.36 percent.
The spread between the two benchmark bonds widened to 36 basis points from 33 basis points at the close of trading on Friday.

Canadian and U.S. bonds opened weaker amid profit taking and a stronger-than-expected U.S. economic report. However, the U.S. market rebounded at the end of the session while Canadian bonds remained weaker amid supply concern.

"It's partly due to the two-year auction on Wednesday and the threat of some provincial and/or corporate paper in the long end coming later in the week," said Jeoff Hall, Canadian market analyst with Boston-based Technical Data.

The Government of Canada on Friday will auction C$3.0 billion in two-year bonds, all of it new cash. In corporate news, Bombardier Inc today said that it planned to file a prospectus for an offering of C$300 million in debentures.
Recent weakness in the Canadian dollar has also weighed on Canadian bonds, dealers said.

Investors shaved half a cent off the Canadian dollar on Friday after disappointing current account data for the third quarter. Further weakness this morning prompted the Bank of Canada to intervene in currency markets, buying Canadian dollars for U.S. dollars.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent of 2006 fell C$0.25 to C$107.10 to yield 6.043 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 3/32 to yield 6.06 percent.
The negative spread between the two narrowed to two basis point from five basis points at Friday's close.
Canada's three-month cash bill traded at 2.76 percent against the U.S. bill at 5.07 percent.
